verdict_label: Minor faux pas, not a real taboo
explanation: Some travel guides warn against showing the soles of your feet in the Philippines by analogy with Thai, Middle Eastern, or South Asian customs, but there is little solid evidence Filipinos treat this as the serious taboo it is in Thailand or Egypt. At most it reads as a bit careless or too casual, similar to putting your feet on furniture in Western etiquette.
local_tip: Don't worry about foot position in most everyday settings, but avoid propping your feet up on furniture or a table when visiting someone's home, especially around elders.
regional_note: In the predominantly Muslim provinces of Mindanao, foot-related modesty norms closer to Islamic etiquette may be observed more strictly.

also_check.note: Feet are considered the lowest part of the body; pointing them at people or Buddha images is a serious offense.
Showing the sole of your shoe or foot is a grave insult, often linked with contempt.
Not a major issue, but feet on furniture or pointing soles at someone can read as overly casual in formal settings.

sources.title: Customs, Greetings and Etiquette: Getting It Right in the Philippines
